newsitem.title: FRANCE: France to decide on welfare deficits in autumn.
newsitem.headline: France to decide on welfare deficits in autumn.

text.p: The French government will decide in the autumn how to tackle accumulated deficits in the welfare system, Finance Minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn said on Monday.
Former prime minister Alain Juppe had warned the incoming Socialist-led government it should tackle the problem in the summer to avoid cash-flow problems in the system.
But Strauss-Kahn told a news conference the question would be considered at the same time as a law on financing for the welfare system and a conference on jobs due in the autumn.
The accumulated deficits in the welfare system, for part of 1996 and this year, are currently funded by temporary advances from state bank Caisse des Depots et Consignations.

Strauss-Kahn confirmed the government had considered introducing now a rise in employer contributions to the welfare system, but had decided against this until all questions on employment were studied at the national jobs conference.
